From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>

Cc: procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: 2025-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: cost assumptions & unit-econ QA for HealthSync eval

Hi Lucy —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. Attached is a first-pass MAP worksheet focused on the cost/unit-econ gating items we discussed (redwood_map_v1.xlsx). Before we lock timelines in the MAP I need a few clarifications so our eval plan and close timeline reflect realistic tokens/$ and operational levers: 

Key assumptions we need answers for (can you reply inline or attach a short note):
- Baseline request profile: average prompt tokens + avg completion tokens per interaction (example: 350 prompt / 120 completion). If you have percentiles (P50/P90) that helps.
- Expected concurrent users and average requests per user / day (or traffic profile CSV). You mentioned some staggered traffic — if you can attach the 7-day profile that’s ideal.
- Caching: which parts of the prompt are static per user (e.g., system instruction, user profile) vs dynamic? Are you able to tolerate a prefix TTL of 1h / 6h / 24h?
- Batching tolerance: what’s acceptable latency SLO for the feature during eval (50ms/100ms/200ms tail)? This dictates batching windows we try in the POC.
- Any encryption/KMS constraints that would prevent KV caching across requests?

Immediate ask: can you provide the traffic CSV and a quick token-per-request estimate by EOD 2025-11-10? We’ll incorporate into the MAP and run a first-cost sketch (tokens/$ at current hosted pricing + caching/batching delta).

Next step I propose: 30-min technical cal on Tuesday 11/11 to align on exact eval gates (prefetch, cache TTL, batching windows) so we can finalize the MAP and push the mutual-action close milestone to 11/28.

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — MAP worksheet (cost items highlighted)

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
chloe@redwood.ai

From: Lucy Zhang <lucy@healthsync.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions & unit-econ QA for HealthSync eval

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for this and for the clear checklist. I attached the traffic profile (healthsync_traffic_profile.csv) and a quick breakdown of our typical interaction:
- Avg prompt tokens: 320 (P50 300 / P90 480)
- Avg completion tokens: 110 (P50 90 / P90 200)
- We expect ~12k active users in week 1 of the pilot, ramping to 45k over 6 weeks. Peak concurrency estimate: 420 concurrent requests.

On caching: we can cache system prompt + user profile fragment (roughly 150 tokens) with a TTL of up to 12 hours. We cannot persist PII in the cache, but deterministic profile bits are fine.

Batching: our UX team prefers sub-150ms tail for interactive flows; background tasks can tolerate higher latency. For the initial eval, target 100ms tail (but we can test relaxed windows in canary).

I’ll have procurement looped if we move the MAP timelines — they’ll need a draft SOW and a list of security artifacts (SOC2 + data flow diagram).

Attachment: healthsync_traffic_profile.csv (csv)

—Lucy

Team — forwarding Lucy’s answers. Two asks: (1) validate tokens/$ sketch and whether our batching/caching proposals are safe given their 100ms interactive SLO; (2) call out any gating items for the MAP that would push the close past 11/28.

Quick notes from me: Lucy confirms ~430 concurrent peak and allow TTL up to 12h for non-PII prefixes (~150 tokens). They expect ramp to 45k users in 6 weeks. I’ve highlighted the cost-sensitive rows in redwood_map_v1.xlsx.

If we can produce an internal cost sketch and a short ops checklist (KV TTL constraints, canary plan for batching, request sampling for P90 tokens) by EOD 11/10, I’ll send back to Lucy with MAP_v2 and updated milestones.

Forwarded message below.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: cost assumptions & unit-econ QA for HealthSync eval

Chloe / team — quick pass from ops/fin perspective. I ran a sketch against hosted pricing and a conservative batching/caching model. Key numbers (attached estimated_costs_v1.csv):
- Baseline tokens per request: 320 + 110 = 430 avg.
- P90 token load ~680 tokens.
- Hosted tokens/$ sketch (no caching, no batching): ~ $0.022 per 1k tokens => rough cost per request = 430 * ($0.022/1000) = $0.00946 (approx).
- With prefix caching (150 tokens) and 50% cache hit at 12h TTL, effective tokens per served request drops ~17% => cost per request ~ $0.0079.
- Batching: moving to a 50ms batching window for interactive queries we can safely batch small groups and reduce GPU cycles, another ~8% savings at typical QPS; 100ms window yields ~12% savings but risks pushing tail. Given their 100ms SLO, I recommend a 50–75ms target window in canary then scale to 100ms for background flows.

Gating items that could delay close:
- If they require 24h availability for prefix cache across regions + encryption-at-rest with HSM per-customer keys, that adds infra work and could slip the 11/28 target (estimate +4–6 weeks).
- If P90 token usage is >800, we need a fallback model variant to keep unit costs bounded.

I attached a simple cost sketch. If we want, I can run a model that includes a quantized endpoint (q4_0) for cheaper per-token cost — that would further reduce unit cost by ~30% on inferencing at the cost of some latency on cold starts.

Attachment: estimated_costs_v1.csv (csv)

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-10T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: cost assumptions & unit-econ QA for HealthSync eval

Folks — product/ops context:
- Canary recommendation: 5% production traffic for 2 weeks with an automated rollback trigger if avg tokens/request delta > +20% or error rate > 1%. This preserves SLA for core users while letting us validate P90 behavior.
- Caching TTL: 12h as Lucy suggested is fine. Ensure cache key excludes PII fields and use customer-scoped namespaces to avoid cross-tenant leaks.
- Batching window: aim for 50ms for the interactive flow at first. We should instrument the tail (P95/P99) and have a per-route override to drop batching if tail crosses 150ms.
- Model variants: prepare a faster, smaller quantized variant (q4_0) for heavy bursts; configure smart routing so >x qps or cost threshold routes to cheaper variant automatically.

MAP gating checklist to include in v2:
- Security artifacts (SOC2 + DFD) uploaded by 11/14 (procurement request)
- Eval traffic CSV validated and signed off by product by 11/10 (Lucy provided but ask for confirmation)
- Canary plan and rollback triggers documented by 11/12
- Cost sketch and deployment runbook by 11/11 (Ben to own)

If we hit these, 11/28 close is realistic. Any infra requests for HSM per-tenant keys will push timeline out.

—Jordan
Director, Solutions Architecture

- Cacheable prefix: ~150 tokens, TTL 12h, cache hit target 50% during pilot.
- Interactive latency SLO: 100ms tail target; canary at 50ms batching window with per-route override if P95 > 150ms.
- Peak concurrency: ~420 requests; initial canary will be 5% of traffic for 2 weeks.
- Model plan: start hosted high-quality variant; enable q4_0 quantized variant for burst routing if cost thresholds exceed projection.

- Redwood (Jordan): canary plan + rollback triggers (due 2025-11-12) — IN PROGRESS.
- Procurement: draft SOW and send security artifact request; HealthSync to provide SOC2/DFD by 2025-11-14.

Proposed timeline: finalize MAP v2 and SOW sign-off by 2025-11-18; begin canary 2025-11-20; target formal close 2025-11-28 if canary meets gates. If HealthSync requires per-tenant HSM keys or cross-region persistent caches, we’ll need to rebaseline (estimate +4–6 weeks).

Attachments: MAP_healthsync_v2.xlsx (xlsx) — includes updated cost rows, gating checklist, and timeline.
